Subject: Westlake pilot: tech stitch, success gates, and next steps

Hi Anna / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the chat today. High-level recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the pilot (3-week evaluation window):

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary goal: reduce triage time for inbound patient queries by surfacing accurate, auditable responses from the knowledge base.
- Must support streaming token delivery into Westlake UI with tool-calling for appointment lookups (API call) and audit logging for each inference (retention 90 days).
- PHI will be present in requests; SOC 2 / encryption controls required.

Proposed pilot scope (what Redwood will deliver):
1) A 3-week pilot environment with a dedicated inference lane (small dedicated capacity) running the X-Lite model variant.
2) SDK + example React streaming client for incremental token rendering and tool-calling hooks for appointment_lookup.
3) Shared success criteria doc and acceptance tests (attached: win_condition_template.xlsx).
4) Security self-attestation and pointer to our SOC 2 report; we will provide evidence and an on-call window for security review.

Initial success gates (we can iterate):
- S1: Average 95th-percentile latency from request to first token <= 450ms for 512-token sessions.
- S2: Tool-call correctness >= 98% on a 200-case sample (appointment lookup).
- S3: No data exfiltration incidents; audit logs accessible to Westlake for the trial window.

Technical ask from your side:
- Confirm engineering owner for integration (name + email).
- Confirm whether streaming must be server-sent events (SSE) or WebSocket.
- Point us at a subset of production-like test data or an API sandbox.

Next steps / timeline:
- By Tue 2027-05-04: confirm owners + sign (or acknowledge) evaluation agreement.
- Wed 2027-05-05: kickoff technical onboarding (30–45 min).
- Week of 2027-05-10: integration sprint (2 weeks), internal validation + acceptance tests.

Attachments: win_condition_template.xlsx (please fill out the acceptance criteria rows so we can lock them).

Would you prefer us to send a DocuSign evaluation agreement or will Westlake use an internal PO first?

Thanks,
Soojin

Attached our initial security questionnaire (westlake_security_questions.pdf) — it's not exhaustive but will help your security team scope the evidence.

DocuSign is fine for the evaluation agreement. Please send; we will sign and return by Monday.

Anna

Hi Anna — quick engineering note on integration approach and a concrete plan for the sprint.

Platform assumptions / proposal:
- We will provide a small Redwood Dedicated lane with pinned model version. Endpoint URL will be: https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/clients/westlake/predict (auth via Bearer token).
- Streaming: we support WebSocket and SSE. We will include a sample React client that uses WebSocket and falls back to SSE if connected behind proxies.
- SDKs: we will provide JS + Python SDKs. For tool-calls, SDK will emit a tool_call event with a correlation_id you can pass back when calling your appointment API.

API surface (examples):
- POST /v1/chat - non-streaming request, returns final response (for batch tests).
- WS /v1/stream - streaming socket; messages are JSON lines with {\"type\":\"token\",\"seq\":int,\"token\":string} and {\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"correlation_id\":string,\"tool\":\"appointment_lookup\",\"payload\":{...}}
- POST /v1/tool-responses - used by Westlake to post tool results to resume generation after tool call.

Latency / load validation:
- We'll run a synthetic replay of 50 concurrent sessions (512 tokens avg) and measure 95th latency to first token. If above 450ms we'll tweak batch sizing/CPU affinity.

Sprint plan (proposed):
- Day 0 (Wed 2027-05-05): kickoff + brief architecture call (30 min).
- Days 1-5: SDK + sample client integration (we provide working sample + docs).
- Days 6-10: instrument audit logs and tool-calling hooks; run internal acceptance tests.
- Days 11-14: Westlake runs acceptance tests (we'll have a shared test harness).

Deliverables and owners:
- Redwood: SDKs, sample client, dedicated endpoint, acceptance test harness (owner: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com).
- Westlake: test data, appointment API sandbox, security sign-off (owner: r.singh@westlakehealth.com / security@westlakehealth.com).

We can support custom correlation_id format; we'll include correlation_id as an optional param in the WS messages.

I'll attach a short checklist after kickoff.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
